sentences.text: Listen to the discussion and write the information in the spaces below.
The first one has been provided as an example.
You now have 30 seconds to study the task.
At the end of the task, you will have one minute to tidy up your answers.
So we've been asked to give our views on this mental mind app.
You know the ones for senior students?
They want us to review it in the magazine.
I've had it on my phone and I've been giving it a go over the weekend.
What's it called?
Mental Mind? Never heard of it.
Not mental, Mental.
Let me show you.
Wait a second till I find it on my phone.
Right. Here it is.
Oh. OK. Right so it, like,
helps you connect with other students from around the world and so they help each other with things like homework and Projects.
Oh, I've heard about this one.
It’s got really good reviews.
So, you're saying you can get help with Projects with this?
Yeah, that's the idea anyway.
Alright, so how do we get started?
Can we have a look at the settings?
Right. settings. Right, here we go.
You try it, Rachel.
Oh, OK. Right.
So see the button with the head and the wheels?
Press it, Right.
Well, here you start by choosing your subjects, your levels for each subject and your modes.
You can select any subjects you like.
Alright, so it looks like there are three starting starting levels: Beginner, Apprentice and Guide.
So, presumably I'd select Guide if I think I know like loads about a subject, and Beginner or Apprentice if I don’t.
Exactly. What about mode What does that mean?
OK, well press it.
so you should see there modes: the first one is Academic.
See? Oh, yeah.
You choose this one if you're preparing for an exam.
The other one is Hobby and it’s for like personal interest only.
Personal interest. Oh, so presumably people can talk about a subject even if they’re not studying for an exam?
What's this one for?
The one the flag.
Is that to choose my country?
Let's try it.
right. Oh, so it looks like there are two settings here: country and.
type of school.
But isn’t it just for secondary schools?
Yeah, it is, But there are different types of schools in different countries.
Like, many they can choose a school for that subject.
Right What's the clock for?
Does it tell the time then?
No, no, this is what they call the office hours setting.
You keeping up, Rachel?
Yes, yes, Right, Office hours.
Ah! Ah, because you're like a professor sitting in your office!
That's clever! So, with this setting, you can choose your availability each day.
You can set a maximum of two hours each weekday to ask and answer live questions, and more on weekends, save three to four hours.
You should set your office hours to when you would normally be doing your homework.
Why do they recommend a set time do you think?
Well, I was thinking about this and I think the first reason is they want to help students develop good time management skills.
Yeah, I have no time management skills whatsoever, I'm such a deadline fighter!
Yeah, no. And the other is that it’s useful for other students to know exactly when you're available.
Because if they know your availability, then they know when you might be able to answer a question.
Make sense. So what are these what are they?
a balloon or something.
Yeah, I have no idea why.
Anyway. you click this button to go to your feedback settings.
Is it each time you help someone they can give you a vote and then write a message to say thanks.
The more votes you get, the thinner you can move up to a higher level.
OK. Yeah, it allows you to show or hide the number of votes you've got as well.
OK. Oh, and I can show or hide the messages I receive from people, you know, the ones that I've helped.
That's pretty cool.
Yeah I know.
I think it’s pretty cool all around actually.
Yeah, it looks useful.
